text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Bedouin held for murders of two young women at Wadi Kelt.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu-Foreign Minister David Levy crisis defused.
- Netanyahu calls Labour leader Ehud Barak "a little man".
- Suicide bomber caught by Palestinian Authority.
- Dollar up 1.6 percent to 3.58 shekels.
- Current account deficit down 26 percent in 1st quarter.
- Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky: High-tech industry to lack 7,000 engineers by 2000.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel: If inflation rises, the interest rate will too. Netanyahu: The exchange rate has changed, just as we promised.
- Accelerated devaluation continues: Dollar soars by 1.59 percent to 3.58 shekels. Devaluation of 4.8 percent within seven days of trading.
HAARETZ
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai working against adding Ariel Sharon to the policymaking team as it's clear Sharon will try to take over and lead.
- Palestinian Authority arrests youth who intended to carry out a suicide attack on Temple Mount.
- U.S. asks Sharon to sign gas deal with Egypt rather than with Russia as it would strengthen peace and it's sensible from an economic standpoint.
- Speculators lose $50 million in eight days of trading due to accelerated devaluation of shekel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- After a late-night meeting Levy and Netanyahu are on the way to a compromise.
- Poll shows that if elections took place today Barak would have the support of 45 percent, Netanyahu 29 percent.
- Sara Netanyahu says that after an interview like the one she gave Israel TV, she feels like leaving Israel.
MAARIV

- Sixty-two percent of Israeli Jews are unhappy with Netanyahu's performance in office, 34 percent satisfied and 4 percent don't know, according to Gallup poll of 500 people this week with a margin of error of 4.5 percent. Mordechai could defeat Barak, poll indicates.
